variants.headline: Building job cancelled part-way
variants.sub: The client has abandoned {project}, which {builder} was building.
variants.body:
The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, has been cancelled part-way because {why}. The client has given up the plan. Readers judging {target} should distinguish this cancellation from a completed handover and consider what responsible stewardship means when an undertaking ends with the work unfinished.

Work does not become imaginary because a client changes the plan. Labour should keep the people and effort involved in view while judging an unfinished undertaking. Cancellation deserves a serious account of responsibility, rather than a story in which the human side of construction disappears once the project loses its purpose.

The stewardship of {target} should be assessed against the part-way cancellation. This paper records the abandoned plan without treating it as proof of a particular financial settlement or a subsequent use for the unfinished work. Ordinary lives should be the measure, not a convenient afterthought.
